focus: Command admission pipeline (metadata, allow-list, scoring compatibility) and harvester scope in both implementations
noveltyJustification: The admission gates, id grammar, uniqueness constraint and harvester code paths are all new evidence; only the bridge existence itself was carried from iteration 1.
keyQuestions: How are commands surfaced to the advisor relative to skills, and do doctor commands participate in that surface at all?
ruledOut: Feeding _routes.yaml to a harvester as a documentation-only change
A one-bridge-per-doctor-route design under the current id grammar

keyFindings.title: Command admission has two inputs: per-skill command-metadata.json or allow-list.json
Command metadata carries userIntent and ownedSignals for plain-word routing
Allow-list entries require id, command, skillId, ownerMode, reason
Bridge id grammar and uniqueness reject multi-target commands like /doctor:git
routingEnabled is per-platform from scoring-compatibility.json; 5 TS-active
Python harvest roots at .skilled/skills with references/assets only
TS harvest mirrors subdir scope behind SPECKIT_ADVISOR_DOC_TRIGGERS
Doc triggers land in skill_docs with content-hash upsert and bounded lane contribution
Neither supported mechanism can read _routes.yaml directly; doctor needs authored metadata
Drift guard and route-validate are the two CI gates any admission change must satisfy
